summary: A fire breaks out on the 800-foot level of the St. Lawrence mine in Butte on the morning of November 23, 1889, after being discovered on the 500-foot level around 4:30 a.m. by a miner named Bell Cuba. Smoke finds its way into the adjoining Anaconda mine, and four miners are reported missing; among the dead is Patrick Murphy, described as married with a wife and nine children and noted as the champion handcar-runner of Montana, who worked alongside his brother Daniel Murphy. The names of others involved in the rescue and disaster include Superintendent Carroll, John Lyons, Harry Page, Tim Kelleher, Jerry Sullivan, Mike Cody, Patrick Cody, James McCarthy, Harry Mannix, and James McCoy.
